sections.h2: What should a seller know about Liberty County, Georgia property tax?
sections.html:
Liberty County is the most densely settled and fastest-growing of the four Georgia counties in the Census comparison, and Hinesville is its seat. Seven taxing areas sit inside the county, each with its own millage rate, so the first thing a seller needs is the area the house is in.

The Census Bureau QuickFacts page counts 70,313 residents in mid-2025, a 7.7 percent rise from the April 2020 base, on 516.47 square miles. Density was 126.3 people per square mile in 2020. Just 50.9 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, the lowest share of the four counties, and median gross rent is $1,246. Median owner-occupied value is $201,500. Builders took out 355 permits in 2025, and 8,042 residents are veterans.

Only 80.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so renters and short-term owners move often. If you are selling a house that has been a rental, the buyer will ask about the tax history and the county's homestead status, so settle both with the offices below before you list.

The rest of the profile is useful context for pricing. QuickFacts counts 23,998 households of about 2.70 people each, a median household income of $60,456 and a per capita income of $28,215. About 51.8 percent of residents 16 and older are in the civilian labor force, workers average a 23.9 minute trip to work, and retail sales in 2022 were about $873.3 million. A household moving in from elsewhere will compare the monthly cost of a mortgage, which the Census puts at a median $1,500 for owners who have one.

sections.h2: Where do I go for a Liberty County tax bill or an assessment question?
sections.html:
Take bills to the tax commissioner and value questions to the assessors; both offices are at 100 Main Street in Hinesville. The commissioner's site accepts online payments and still takes payment in person or by mail at 100 Main Street, Suite 1545, Hinesville, GA 31313. Its phone number is 912-876-3389.

The Assessors Office is at 100 Main Street, Suite 1550, and answers at 912-876-3568. The phone menu from the county handout splits the work:

  • Option 1: administration, which covers homesteads and general information.
  • Option 2: mapping, GIS and specialized assessment.
  • Option 3: personal property, including prebill mobile homes, vehicles, boats, business inventory, aircraft and commercial property.
  • Option 4: real property appraisers.

The county's Official Assessment Documents page lets you pull a property record card or a real property assessment notice by typing a parcel number, with a separate search if you do not know yours. The assessors also take email at Tax.Assessors@libertycountyga.gov.

sections.h2: What are the proposed 2026 millage rates in Liberty County?
sections.html:
The county commissioners proposed 19.4000 mills for the unincorporated area and lower rates inside most cities. The figures below come from the county's press release on the proposed 2026 increase, so your bill is the final word on the rate that applies.

Proposed 2026 Liberty County millage rates, per the county press release
AreaProposed county mills
Unincorporated area19.4000
Hinesville17.3350
Flemington17.5590
Walthourville17.7745
Midway17.8746
Riceboro17.8446
Allenhurst and Gumbranch19.4000

The release says the proposal raised the levy by 1.32 percent in the unincorporated area and 6.15 percent in Hinesville, and that Midway and Riceboro show 100 percent only because both cities adopted a municipal rate for the first time in 2026. Floating Local Option Sales Tax proceeds from January to June lowered the calculated rollback rates by roughly 1.6520 mills. Three public hearings were set on the proposed increase, two on November 3 and one on November 12, 2026, at the county annex on North Main Street. Those dates have passed.

The same release prints the final rollback rates, which are the levels that would raise the same revenue as last year on the new digest: 19.1460 mills for the unincorporated area, 16.3300 for Hinesville, 17.6830 for Flemington and 18.9030 for Walthourville. Where the proposed rate is above the rollback rate, state law requires the hearings. Ask the commissioner's office for the adopted rate once the board votes, since that is the number your bill will use.

sections.h2: How do assessment notices and appeals work in Liberty County?
sections.html:
Notices arrive in May and you have 45 days from the notice date to appeal. The county handout points out that the notice is not a bill, and the deadline is printed on the notice itself.

The calendar the assessors publish looks like this:

  • Homestead applications and real property returns: January 1 to April 1.
  • Prebill mobile home bills: mailed around February 1, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Annual notices of assessment: mailed in May, with 45 days to appeal.
  • Personal property returns: mailed around December 22 and returned between January 1 and April 1.

Taxes themselves are not qualifying grounds for an appeal. Owners with 10 acres or more of agricultural, forestry or environmentally sensitive land may qualify for a specialized assessment, and the mapping option on the phone menu handles that and any splitting or combining of parcels.

Expect a visit. Staff inspect a property after a homestead application, a return, an appeal, a purchase or a permit, and when it has not been seen in more than three years. They measure, photograph and note features. State code 48-5-264.1 lets appraisers go onto land outside the buildings, and they are expected to carry visible identification.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption work for a Liberty County home?
sections.html:
You qualify if you own the land and the home and live in it, and the application deadline is April 1 of each year. Call 912-876-3568 and press 1 to ask what documents to bring.

Georgia's general rule, from the Department of Revenue, is that assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value and the standard state exemption is $2,000 taken off that assessed figure before the millage rate is applied. Many counties add local exemptions, so ask the administration desk whether Liberty County has any that are bigger. Because the area millage differs, the same exemption saves a Hinesville owner a different amount than an owner in the unincorporated area.

For a seller, the exemption stays with the seller's ownership, not with the house. A buyer who plans to live in the property should apply as soon as they close and no later than April 1 of the first tax year they own and live in it.

sections.h2: What should I do about taxes when I sell in Liberty County?
sections.html:
Find out whether the year's bill is issued and paid, then settle the split at closing. Georgia's Department of Revenue says the owner on January 1 is responsible for the full year and that no refund is available to a partial-year owner.

The commissioner's online system lets you search property records and pay, which is useful when a buyer's lender wants proof of payment. Census figures show about half of the county's housing units are owner-occupied, so a tenant may well live in the home you are selling; if one does, give the buyer the lease and the tax status together. Call 912-876-3389 for any open balance and ask your closing attorney to account for it.

faqs.q: Who values property in Liberty County?
faqs.a: The Liberty County Assessors Office values it, at 100 Main Street, Suite 1550 in Hinesville. Call 912-876-3568 and press 4 to reach the real property appraisers.

faqs.q: What is the Liberty County homestead deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 of each year. The assessors' handout also gives January 1 to April 1 as the window for real property returns.

faqs.q: Is a Liberty County assessment notice a bill?
faqs.a: No. It explains the appraised and assessed value of the property, and the 45 day appeal period runs from the date on the notice.

faqs.q: How can I look up my Liberty County assessment?
faqs.a: Use the county's Official Assessment Documents page and enter your parcel number to see the record card or the assessment notice.

faqs.q: Does Liberty County use a sales tax to cut property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The 2026 press release says Floating Local Option Sales Tax proceeds collected from January to June lowered the rollback millage rates by about 1.6520 mills.
